result: One of the two perchlorate anions (Cl2) is disordered, and I submitted a model with that disorder included. In the original ordered model, the strongest difference peaks (0.6–0.9 e/Å³) all sat about 0.9 Å from O6, O7 and O8 of this anion. Those three atoms also had large, very anisotropic displacement parameters (Ueq 0.064–0.076, largest-to-smallest ratio up to 7). Three of the peaks lie about 1.3–1.5 Å from Cl2 at roughly tetrahedral angles to each other and to O5. That points to a second orientation of the anion, rotated about the Cl2–O5 bond. I kept O5 shared and split O6, O7 and O8 into PART 1 and PART 2, with occupancies tied to a free variable that refined to 0.70/0.30. I restrained the geometry with SADI on the Cl–O and O···O distances and the displacement parameters with SIMU and RIGU. R1 dropped from 0.0341 to 0.0332 and wR2 from 0.0915 to 0.0900, and the split ADPs became much more reasonable. Some smaller peaks (about 0.6–0.8 e/Å³) remain near this anion, which may mean the disorder is slightly more complex than two orientations. I left those unmodelled, and I didn't change any other part of the structure.
